texts: The right fibrous trigone is part of the central fibrous body, the heart's keystone, which it forms together with the membranous septum: A.
The fibrous skeleton holds the valves; the right and left trigones, the stone triangles, anchor the anterior mitral leaflet and the aortic valve.
The mitral annulus is saddle-shaped, highest at its anterior and posterior midpoints and lowest at the commissures, and it gets smaller, not bigger, in systole.

First-order chordae, tied to the free edges, prevent prolapse; second-order chordae hold the body of the leaflets and help keep the ventricle's shape; and the anterolateral papillary muscle usually has one head, the posteromedial several.
Memory hook: Sogeking's pebble hits the right triangle, and the whole keystone rings as one stone.
